obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (retail merchant account)
citation: Retail merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected compromise of brand card data, including a common point of purchase notice from the acquirer or processor
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). The clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
notify: Acquirer merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
notifying_entity: Grocery Retail (payments director with the Grocery Retail CISO)

obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (wholesale merchant account)
citation: Wholesale merchant agreement (fictional term, same as the retail term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data entered on the Retailer Services Portal payment page
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term)
notify: Acquirer for the wholesale merchant account
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the acquirer, not law. If the business accepts American Express, the DSOP (April 2026, Section 3) requires notice to American Express within 72 hours of discovery. Mastercard and Discover rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the acquirer immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquirer; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquirer. Other brands as the acquirer directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; Mastercard and Discover rules were not verified
clock_starts: Suspicion or confirmation of the compromise

obligation: Internal notice from the group SOC to each affected division
trigger: The SOC declares a Severity 1 incident on a payment page of any division
deadline: Immediately on the incident bridge
notify: Grocery Retail CISO; Grocery Wholesale security and compliance lead; Financial Services CISO (Qualified Individual)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - group policy

obligation: Third-party agent notice from Grocery Retail to Financial Services (Rewards Card data)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (worked example; other states' third-party duties vary)
trigger: Breach of Rewards Card data that Grocery Retail collects on its checkout page on behalf of Financial Services
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the runbook gives notice on the bridge on Day 0
notify: Financial Services (Qualified Individual and chief compliance officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Grocery Retail acts as Financial Services' agent for the Rewards Card field

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without authorization (presumed from unauthorized access unless reliable evidence shows otherwise, 314.2) involving at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC through the online form on ftc.gov (name and contact, types of information, dates, number of consumers, description, any law enforcement delay request)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Financial Services is a financial institution under Part 314; Rewards Card numbers and codes are customer information
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known to any employee, officer, or agent (314.4(j)(2)); the runbook treats the group SOC's knowledge as Financial Services' discovery

obligation: Law enforcement delay of public disclosure after the FTC notice
trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or harm national security
deadline: Initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice; up to 60 more days on a written request; longer only if FTC staff agree
notify: Include the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Red Flags response for compromised Rewards Card accounts
trigger: Red Flags detected (compromised account numbers and codes)
deadline: Respond appropriately to prevent and mitigate identity theft (no fixed deadline); the program sets the steps
notify: Affected cardholders through account alerts; card processing platform
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Financial Services is a creditor with covered accounts

obligation: Block and reissue compromised Rewards Cards
citation: 12 CFR 1026.12(a)(2) (a card may be issued as a renewal of or substitute for an accepted card without a request); card processing platform agreement
trigger: Rewards Card numbers in the exposure window
deadline: No legal deadline; target within 5 days of the account list (runbook)
notify: Card processing platform (block and reissue); affected cardholders
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Cardholder liability limit for unauthorized use
trigger: Fraudulent charges on a compromised Rewards Card
deadline: Cardholder liability may not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained before notice to the issuer
notify: Cardholders (in account letters and service scripts)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Billing error resolution for disputed fraudulent charges
trigger: A cardholder's written billing error notice received within 60 days after the first statement showing the charge (1026.13(b))
deadline: Written acknowledgment within 30 days of receipt; resolve within 2 complete billing cycles and no later than 90 days
notify: The cardholder who sent the notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan capacity for a surge in disputes (P03 FS-G39)
clock_starts: Receipt of each billing error notice

obligation: State data breach notification (all affected individuals)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents (definitions vary; card number with security code and name is covered in most states)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (6 southeastern states for retail shoppers; 8 states for wholesale customers; any state for online shoppers who live elsewhere)
notifying_entity: Grocery Retail (brand card data); Financial Services (Rewards Card data); Grocery Wholesale (personal cards of independent grocers)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents: name with a credit or debit card number and any required security code (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. 15 more days are available for this notice only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed card numbers with security codes
notifying_entity: Grocery Retail; Financial Services; Grocery Wholesale (each for its own customers)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Grocery Retail and Financial Services each exceed 500 Florida residents in the exercise scenario

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Grocery Retail and Financial Services

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies; keep the request in writing
notify: Hold individual notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the entity reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination, keep it 5 years, and give it to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides

obligation: Independent grocer contract notice
citation: Independent grocer supply agreement, 2024 form (fictional term)
trigger: Security incident affecting the customer's data or payment information
deadline: Within 72 hours after the division confirms the incident
notify: Each affected independent grocer's designated contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
clock_starts: Confirmation of the incident by the division

obligation: State EBT processor contact
citation: State EBT processor agreements (not verified in this sample)
trigger: EBT card data involved (for example PIN pad skimming in stores)
deadline: Per each state agreement; confirm before use
notify: State EBT processor for each affected state
applies_at_this_tier: Only if EBT data is involved; not in this exercise scenario (EBT is accepted in stores only)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Company Holdings is an SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay (POL-03 4.7)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - lessons from the incident may inform the risk management and governance description

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement
trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data
deadline: As soon as practicable (target Day 0 to Day 2)
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; supports a law enforcement delay request if one is needed

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand (for example a threat to publish skimmed data)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons
notifying_entity: Group (Group General Counsel; board risk committee approval under POL-03 4.8)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until then

obligation: HIPAA breach notification
trigger: Breach of unsecured protected health information
deadline: n/a
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group has no pharmacy and no other HIPAA covered function

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts (P03)
